engagement_background.objective: Advantia Health engaged Treya Partners to identify and capture cost-savings across its spend base, strengthen procurement processes, and support value-creation objectives by delivering $0.7-$1.4 million in annual savings through strategic sourcing.
engagement_background.scope_summary: Treya is addressing 10 spend categories representing roughly $19 million in addressable spend (out of ~$45 million total AP/P-card spend), plus a review of procurement processes and operational controls; optional work on Employee Benefits was scheduled for a later phase.
constraints_challenges: Limited strategic procurement resources and focus prior to the engagement
Spend and contract data spread across two AP systems (Advantia Mid-Atlantic and Heartland) with incomplete line-item detail
Supplier fragmentation and long-standing incumbent relationships across multi-site clinics, making change management sensitive
Requirement to avoid parallel purchasing activity during the project to prevent market confusion
Six-month target timeline (excluding Benefits) places pressure on data collection, sourcing cycles, and implementation

procurement_environment.data_availability: AP and P-card header-level data from two systems were available; contracts and detailed usage data had to be requested from key suppliers.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: No centralized contract repository; inconsistent supplier naming and limited item-level usage details—some suppliers did not provide data even after multiple requests.
